CVSS: attacker = MCP server operator (remote party). AV: network? The agent runs locally as CLI; MCP server is remote on internal lab network... Adjacent network? Compose lab internal network; MCP server attacker-controlled/compromised — network-reachable. AV:N or A. The lab network is internal; agent joins egress only for model API. MCP server in compose network → adjacent. I'd say AV:A (limited to shared logical network) — actually attacker must control/compromise MCP server, which is on the internal lab network. AV:A.

AC: L. AT: P (requires being connected to attacker's MCP server — a condition attacker can't force? Precondition states the agent must be connected to attacker-controlled server). PR: N? Attacker is server operator, not authenticated user of the agent. PR:N. UI: P passive — user must ask the agent to email. Actually requires user to request email task: passive (using system normally). UI:P.

VC: N? Email content delivered to attacker → confidentiality of agent's email content compromised. Vulnerable system is the agent process; the data (email) going to attacker — VC:L. VI: integrity? Email never passes through agent's tool — L? Data rerouting: VI:L. VA: N. SC:N, SI? Subsequent: recipient/intended email system? SI:L maybe. Keep SC:N SI:L SA:N? Simpler: VC:L/VI:N/VA:N, SC:N/SI:N/SA:N. Hmm email content delivered to attacker is confidentiality loss of vulnerable system: VC:L. VI:N.

AIVSS: LC=D (attacker-supplied description/tool manifest influences tool invocation... manifest text reaches model and steers which tool is called → Direct). CP: S? Manifest refetched each run but not persistent attacker memory; shadowing occurs per-run — session context. CP:S? Manifest isn't persistent durable store; CP:N? Attacker context persists across runs since manifest refetched every run... but that's the server, not stored memory. CP:S (session) or N. I'll say S.
AP: C (relay into remote server component — crossing to attacker's server is downstream impact). AP:C? Actually influence relays across agent components same principal; the call routes to remote server = crossing trust boundary to attacker's server → lateral? "Impact on downstream systems scored in CVSS." AP:C.
RH: reachability of proxy/evaluator? No evidence → X. reachable_proxy null, isolation_verified null → X.
ES: W (unvetted dynamic remote tools, manifest trusted unpinned).
